message.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    This article develops the concept of
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Dreamy Stacks</jats:italic>
                    to analyze how India's Digital Public Infrastructures (DPIs) and the
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Startup India</jats:italic>
                    program are reconfiguring relations between the state, citizens, and techno-capitalism. It shows how the post-Aadhaar state increasingly renders itself as a stack of data layers that promises digital and financial inclusion, interoperability, and innovation, even as these infrastructures remain materially fragmented, failure-prone, and dependent on public subsidy. Through a relational and intermedial ethnographic approach to data infrastructures, the article maps how the promise of DPIs depends on tethering data-driven governance to entrepreneurial aspiration. Drawing on long-term ethnographic research in Rajasthan, it examines how “Rajasthan Stack”—a regional analogue of India Stack—is imagined, circulated, and only partially materialized as a set of Application Programming Interfaces and platforms. Attending to the disjuncture between promissory visions and lived experience, the article shows how the state-driven expansion of start-ups, incubators, and data centers in small cities re-spatializes global techno-futurity beyond metropolitan centers. Challenging universalist accounts that privilege scale, seamless platforms, formal markets, and stable data-value relations,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Dreamy Stacks</jats:italic>
                    names a coeval, speculative, state-mediated architecture of futurity and failure through which global techno-capitalism is made unevenly, partially, and in practice.
                  </jats:p>
title: Dreamy Stacks: Digital Public Infrastructure, Futurity, and Failure in Startup India
